messages:
meera: FYI customer reporting repeated mid-stream SSE disconnects during carrier -> WiFi handoffs. They see partial chunks delivered, then connection closes and client reports ECONNRESET/499. Attaching short client log and a pcap.

alex: thanks — can you paste the client-side log snippet and the request id we should look for on the edge? Also, which SDK/version are they using?

meera: client logs (redacted):
```
[2026-02-04T14:12:11.213Z] SSE stream start id=rc_7a2b
[2026-02-04T14:12:15.891Z] recv chunk: {"id":"rc_7a2b","choices":[{"delta":"Hello"}],"done":false}
[2026-02-04T14:12:18.002Z] network change: WWAN->WiFi
[2026-02-04T14:12:18.310Z] client socket closed (errno=104) -> ECONNRESET
[2026-02-04T14:12:18.315Z] partial chunk received, stream aborted
```
Request-id in header: x-rw-request-id: rw-9f34a2e1\nSDK: mobile-js v2.3.1\n```
\nalex: log shows client closes immediately after network change (FIN/RST). That's client-side termination, not our runtime timing out. iOS TCP stack often tears down TLS when switching networks. Two quick checks: 1) does the client re-open a brand-new SSE connection and request resume (our SDK supports resume via ids)? 2) are they running any aggressive app-level timeouts (e.g., abort controller with <5s)?

jordan: we had a case like this last quarter. Recommendations we gave the app team: add application-level keepalive pings (a lightweight comment event) every 10-15s, and on network-change do a graceful reconnect flow that retries resume with the last-event-id. Also ensure the underlying socket keepalive is configured shorter than platform default (mobile OS defaults are very long).

meera: customer claims they already send heartbeats every 30s. Their pcap shows the client sending a FIN immediately at the link-change, not idle. They want to know if any edge/proxy config could be forcibly closing the socket on a NAT rebinding. Edge logs for rw-9f34a2e1:
```
[edge] rw-9f34a2e1 ACCEPT from 52.14.22.8:52344
[edge] rw-9f34a2e1 upstream conn established
[edge] rw-9f34a2e1 stream chunk sent 14:12:15
[edge] rw-9f34a2e1 upstream: read failed: connection reset by peer
[edge] rw-9f34a2e1 stream terminated, code=client_reset
```
\nalex: edge sees client_reset too. That aligns with client-initiated FIN/RST. Still useful to repro: can you ask them to run Network Link Conditioner (or change network) while curling the SSE and capture tcpdump on device? For repro on our side, we can simulate with tc/netem to flip IP and force NAT rebinding.

jordan: repro steps for eng-runtime:
1) Start an SSE stream from a test client: `curl -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -N \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=small\" > /dev/null &`
2) After 10s, on the client host run: `sudo ip route change default via <new-gateway>` or use `tc qdisc`/`ifconfig` to down/up the interface to trigger a network rebind.`
3) Observe if client issues FIN/RST and whether the edge logs `client_reset` or we see any `proxy_read_timeout`. Capture pcap on client and edge.

meera: customer already ran a pcap. Their trace shows FIN from client within ~300ms of network-change. They also mentioned using a third-party VPN which may be tearing sessions.

alex: next actions:
- Meera: confirm whether SDK resume logic was enabled and what last-event-id was used. If they don't resume, advise implementing exponential reconnect with last-event-id.
- Jordan: try the netem repro on staging and see if any of our proxies (envoy/nginx) treat the midstream NAT rebinding as a connection error we can mitigate (we can test keepalive settings and `proxy_protocol` behaviour).
- If repro shows server-side resets, escalate to eng-runtime with pcap + edge logs + request id.

sre-bot: Created support ticket SUP-2026-174 and linked to eng-runtime channel `eng-runtime` (INC-2026-512).

meera: I'll collect the full pcap, SDK config, and ask the customer to verify behavior without the VPN. Will update thread once we have the device pcap uploaded. If they still see immediate FINs we'll escalate with the artifacts. :thumbsup:
